output.answer: Yes. The most recent verified announcement is a planned layoff of 118 employees tied to the permanent closure of the Post’s Springfield, Virginia, printing plant; the company’s Oct. 7 WARN notice says separations were expected by Dec. 31, 2026 or within 14 days thereafter ([Virginia Works WARN notice](https://virginiaworks.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Washington-Post-Springfield-VA-Plant-Closure-WARN-Notice.pdf); [FFXnow](https://www.ffxnow.com/2026/10/15/washington-post-plans-layoffs-ahead-of-springfield-printing-plant-closure/)). Earlier, on Feb. 4, the Post announced a broader restructuring affecting roughly one-third of the company, including major newsroom reductions ([TheWrap](https://www.thewrap.com/media-platforms/journalism/washington-post-layoffs-jeff-bezos-2/); [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/02/04/media/washington-post-layoffs)).
caveats: The 118-job figure concerns the Springfield printing-plant closure and is separate from the broader February newsroom/company cuts.
The February announcement did not provide an exact company-wide headcount in the opened sources; “roughly one-third” and “about one in three” are the reported proportions.
The WARN notice describes planned separations; it does not establish that every listed separation had occurred by the as-of date.

passages.quote: This notice is to inform you that WP Company LLC (“The Post”) is closing its Springfield, Virginia facility... The entire facility will be closed. This facility closure will unfortunately result in the separation of various employees. The Post expects this action to be permanent.
The Post anticipates that the date of the first separation will be December 31, 2026 and that affected employees will be separated by December 31, 2026 or within fourteen days thereafter.
The Washington Post announced plans on Wednesday to significantly downsize the paper... one-third of the company, which includes the newsroom, is impacted.
The Washington Post laid off about one in three employees across the company Wednesday morning.

output.question: Has The Washington Post announced layoffs?

key_facts.fact: The Washington Post filed a WARN notice dated Oct. 7, 2026, stating that its Springfield, Virginia, facility would close permanently and that affected employees would be separated by Dec. 31, 2026, or within 14 days thereafter.
The WARN notice lists 118 affected employees.
The Post announced a February 2026 restructuring affecting one-third of the company, including reductions to international, metro, sports and books coverage.
CNN reported that the February 2026 cuts affected about one in three employees across the company.
